answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded web of trust: each agent posts a stake and earns vouchers from distinct, admitted identities, so trust grows like a vine from a few rooted accounts. A fake cluster has no honest roots; to get vouched, each new node must bribe or compromise a separate member, so the attacker's cost scales with honest signers, not with how many nodes it creates. Honest members broadcast a signed signal of their voucher count, letting peers prune dense clusters. Even a zephyr of cheap bots fails, because the bottleneck is scarce endorsements, making a Sybil farm costly.
